newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil extends coffee producers' debts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil extends coffee producers' debts.

text.p: Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) Thursday approved a 7-1/2-year extension to 212 million reais in coffee producers' debts, officials said.
A Finance Ministry official said the CMN had agreed to the extension in the maturity of non-securitized debt to the state's Funcafe coffee fund.
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce said there was an 18-month grace period.
An initial 10 percent of the debt would have been paid in 18 months, with the balance divided into 15-percent instalments payable over six years, a ministry official said.
The government will charge producers its Long-Term Interest Rate (TJLP) plus three percent a year.
The industry's total debt is thought to be about 581 million reais, with the rest being securitized Funcafe loans and loans from state-run Banco do Brasil or from private banks.
The renegotiation of the non-securitized portion of the Funcafe debt had been on the cards for about three months.
